findings.source_quote: διὸ πρὸς τοὺς σώζειν αὐτοὺς δυναμένους ἐλθεῖν ὀκνηρότεροι γίνονται καὶ τοὺς ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐνεδρευόντων δαιμόνων ἀναλισκόμενοι ἀγνοοῦσιν.
findings.english_quote: Therefore they become more reluctant to go to those capable of saving them, and, while being consumed by the very demons lying in wait for them, they remain unaware.
findings.issue: The English supplies no object for ἀγνοοῦσιν and no English value for the surviving accusative τοὺς. The source note assumes that τοὺς should agree with ἀναλισκόμενοι, but it can instead be considered an anaphoric accusative object of ἀγνοοῦσιν, referring back to those capable of saving them. On that reading, the nominative participle describes the people who fail to recognize those helpers. The note's proposed deletion therefore does not establish fidelity to the supplied reading. This problem is separate from the four-dot lacuna, which the draft faithfully represents and discloses.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Therefore they become more reluctant to go to those capable of saving them, and, while being consumed by the very demons lying in wait for them, they fail to recognize them.” Explain that the final “them” takes τοὺς anaphorically as referring to those capable of saving them, and preserve any viable referent alternatives. Revise the source note so that it does not present agreement with the participle as obligatory. This candidate requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ εἰς τέλος κολασθησομένας καθιστᾶσιν τῶν ἀνακεκραμένων τὰς ἠπατημένας αὐτοῖς ψυχάς
findings.english_quote: they put the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them in a state of being punished to the end
findings.issue: κολασθησομένας is a future passive participle: the souls will undergo punishment. “In a state of being punished” instead presents punishment as an already operative state. The lexical note discusses the extent expressed by εἰς τέλος but does not address this loss of prospective force.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the quoted phrase with a prospective formulation, such as “they bring it about that the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them will be punished to the end.” Retain the disclosed alternatives concerning the extent of εἰς τέλος and the subject of χωρήσαντες. The revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: πόσοις κατ’ ὄναρ ὁμοίως ἄλλοις ὤφθησαν καὶ ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις πρὸς τὸ κατ’ ὄναρ ἀντιβάλλοντες οὐ συνεφώνησαν;
findings.english_quote: To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams, yet when those people met one another while awake and compared what they had seen in the dream, they did not agree?
findings.issue: The draft makes disagreement the circumstance being counted and introduces an adversative “yet.” The Greek coordinates the appearances and subsequent comparison with καί and ends in a negative question, οὐ συνεφώνησαν; its contextual rhetorical force is “did they not agree?” The following inference that the experience is no longer merely a dream supports agreement, not the draft's presentation of disagreement.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “To how many others have they appeared similarly in dreams, and have those people not agreed when they met one another while awake and compared their dream experiences?” Preserve the negative question explicitly and remove the unsupported adversative “yet.” The revised question requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας
findings.english_quote: with the soul giving the forms back to the paria fears and to desire
findings.issue: “Paria” is a transliteration, not an established English rendering of παρίᾳ. No defensible meaning or construction connecting this surviving word with τοῖς ... φόβοις has been supplied. The draft correctly discloses this obstacle, but disclosure cannot make the untranslated wording publishable. The block concerns unresolved meaning in verified print, not unavailable wording in a printed lacuna or the mere existence of interpretive alternatives.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep this passage blocked until a documented lexical and grammatical account supports an English rendering of the exact printed phrase. Any proposed emendation must quote παρίᾳ separately from the proposed correction and must not be presented as the supplied reading or as recovered wording. Rechecking the already verified print alone would not resolve the meaning problem.

findings.source_quote: ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα, διὰ ὀνείρων τὰς ἰδέας ἀποκυΐσκει.
findings.english_quote: Or, when struck in its mind by fear, it gives birth to the forms through dreams.
findings.issue: The main text represents the printed disjunctive ἢ but omits the explanatory γάρ. The source note includes “For” only in its conjectural alternative with ἡ; that does not cover γάρ in the supplied reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Represent both particles without adopting the conjecture, for example: “For, alternatively, when its mind has been struck by fear, it gives birth to the forms through dreams.” Retain the note distinguishing printed ἢ from proposed ἡ. This revision requires fresh review.
